notes: Saudi Arabia: Persian Gulf fields to Yanbu on the Red Sea. Only carries Saudi crude; near-zero extra transit time since it was headed toward Red Sea/Suez shipping lanes anyway. Estimate.
UAE: Habshan fields to Fujairah on the Gulf of Oman, entirely outside Hormuz. Near-zero extra transit time. Estimate.

No pipeline exists for Iranian (Kharg Island) or Qatari (Ras Laffan) crude -- only option is sailing around Africa instead of through Hormuz. Unlimited capacity (any tanker can do it) but adds ~10-14 days transit for Persian Gulf-to-Europe/Americas routes. Estimate.
Egypt: Ain Sukhna (Red Sea) to Sidi Kerir (Mediterranean), the standard overland bypass when the Canal itself is blocked or congested. Near-zero extra transit time. Estimate.

For traffic the SUMED pipeline can't absorb (its throughput is well below Suez's ~9M bpd total oil flow). Unlimited capacity but adds ~8-10 days for Asia/Gulf-to-Europe routes. Estimate (2021 Ever Given blockage precedent).

Indonesia: deeper-water alternate south of Malacca, used by very large crude carriers (VLCCs) too big for some Malacca shallows. Real route, not a diversion -- adds only ~1-2 days. Estimate.
